## baggr

_baggr_ (Bayesian aggregator) is a new R package for Bayesian meta-analysis models that uses Stan

_baggr_ beta is available on [CRAN](https://cran.r-project.org/package=baggr) and [GitHub](https://github.com/wwiecek/baggr)



## Motivation and goals

Our goals: 

1. Implement all basic Bayesian meta-analysis models and tools
2. Focus on accessibility, model criticism and comparison
3. Help people avoid basic mistakes
4. Keep the framework flexible and extend to more models

(Probably) _not_ our goal:

5. Build a package for people who already build their models in Stan



## Walk through a simple example (8 schools!)

After Rubin (1981)\footnote{Rubin, Donald B. "Estimation in Parallel Randomized Experiments". Journal of Educational Statistics 6, no. 4 (1981): 377–401.}

* Assume only aggregate data available 
* Bayesian hierarchical model. Each study measures pair $(y_i, se_i)$:
    + $y_i \sim \mathcal{N}(\tau_i, se_i)$
* Upper level:
    + $\tau_i \sim \mathcal{N}(\tau, \sigma)$
* $\sigma = 0$ is "full pooling", $\sigma = \infty$ is "no pooling"; otherwise partial pooling.
* We need a prior on $\sigma$, $\tau$; $se_i$ treated as known.


## Why go Bayesian with meta-analysis?

Beyond "vanilla" arguments. In the package:

- Incorporate prior beliefs (uniquely suitable to meta-analysis)
- Avoid problems with underestimated variance
- Emphasis on uncertainty (also in heterogeneity)
- Interpretability and ease of creating predictive distributions
- Work with derived quantities (e.g. $\text{Pr}(\forall_i: \tau_i > x)$)
- Easy model comparison

Cost of this: computation, model checking, higher technological barrier to entry etc.

- Flexible (code your model "by hand")

## Starting analysis

\small

- You need `rstan` and `baggr` packages in R. 
- No extra software needed, but you need RTools.


```{r, echo = T}
library(baggr)
schools
```

(Code for individual-level data would look almost identical.)

## _baggr_  syntax example: simple model workflow

\tiny 

```{r, eval = T, include = F, cache = T}
# Fitting function is baggr()
fit <- baggr(schools, model = "rubin", pooling = "partial",
             prior_hypermean = normal(0, 25), prior_hypersd = uniform(0, 100))

# Automatic prior choice, automatic model choice (with prompts):
eff_lab <- "mean SAT improvement"
niter <- 1e04 #to make it a bit smoother in slides
fit_c <- baggr(schools, prior_hypersd = cauchy(0, 2.5), effect = eff_lab,
               iter = niter)
fit_n <- baggr(schools, prior_hypersd = normal(0, 5), effect = eff_lab,
               iter = niter)
fit_u <- baggr(schools, prior_hypersd = uniform(0, 100),
                        prior_hypermean = normal(-5, 10), effect = eff_lab,
               iter = niter)

# Plot results for one model, making use of bayesplot
baggr_theme_update(text = element_text(family = "mono"))
plot(fit_c, style = "areas", hyper = TRUE, order = TRUE)

# Compare fit to data
bgc <- baggr_compare("Cauchy" = fit_c, "Normal" = fit_n, "Uniform" = fit_u)
bgc; plot(bgc)
# Compare posterior predictive distribution (note ggplot)
effect_plot("Cauchy" = fit_c, "Normal" = fit_n, "Uniform" = fit_u) + xlim(-10, 30)

# Compare the impact of different prior choices
bgc_pooling <- baggr_compare(schools, prior_hypersd = normal(0, 10), what = "pooling")
plot(bgc_pooling)

# Use LOO cross-validation to choose between partial & full pooling
loo_p <- loocv(schools, pooling = "partial")
loo_f <- loocv(schools, pooling = "full")
loo_compare(loo_p, loo_f)
```

```{r, eval = F, include = T}
# Fitting function is baggr()
fit <- baggr(schools, model = "rubin", pooling = "partial",
             prior_hypermean = normal(0, 25), prior_hypersd = uniform(0, 100))

# Semi-automatic prior choice, automatic model choice (with prompts):
eff_lab <- "mean SAT improvement"
fit_c <- baggr(schools, prior_hypersd = cauchy(0, 2.5), effect = eff_lab)
fit_n <- baggr(schools, prior_hypersd = normal(0, 5), effect = eff_lab)
fit_u <- baggr(schools, prior_hypersd = uniform(0, 100),
                        prior_hypermean = normal(-5, 10), effect = eff_lab)

# Plot results for one model, making use of bayesplot
baggr_theme_update(text = element_text(family = "mono"))
plot(fit_c, style = "areas", hyper = TRUE, order = TRUE)

# Compare fit to data
bgc <- baggr_compare("Cauchy" = fit_c, "Normal" = fit_n, "Uniform" = fit_u)
bgc; plot(bgc)
# Compare posterior predictive distribution (note ggplot)
effect_plot("Cauchy" = fit_c, "Normal" = fit_n, "Uniform" = fit_u) + xlim(-10, 30)

# Compare the impact of different prior choices
bgc_pooling <- baggr_compare(schools, prior_hypersd = normal(0, 10), what = "pooling")
plot(bgc_pooling)

# Use LOO cross-validation to choose between partial & full pooling
loo_p <- loocv(schools, pooling = "partial")
loo_f <- loocv(schools, pooling = "full")
loo_compare(loo_p, loo_f)
```
